title: Rhyming Basket
strapline: Cat, hat, mat — hearing the sounds inside words, the secret door to reading.
intent: Children tune their ears to rhyme — hearing that words can sound the same at the end — a key early-reading skill.
Children play with the sounds of language, building the phonological awareness that reading later builds on.
Children enjoy the rhythm, silliness and music of rhyming words and nursery rhymes.
Children learn new vocabulary through the concrete objects that a rhyming basket holds.
Children begin to generate their own rhymes, even nonsense ones, showing they've cracked the pattern.
implementation: Fill a basket with real objects that rhyme in pairs or families — cat/hat, sock/rock, spoon/moon, star/car.
Pull out objects and name them slowly, stretching the sounds so the rhyme is easy to hear.
Play matching games: 'can you find something that rhymes with cat?' and celebrate the find.
Sing the nursery rhymes the objects belong to, pausing before the rhyming word for children to fill in.
Welcome nonsense rhymes — 'cat, hat, zat, plat!' — as evidence children have heard the pattern.
Model 'odd one out' gently: 'cat, hat, dog — which one doesn't rhyme?'
Keep sessions short, playful and oral — no letters or reading needed, just ears and voices.
key_questions: Can you find something that rhymes with 'cat'?
Which two of these sound the same at the end?
What rhymes with 'moon' — even a silly word?
Can you finish the rhyme: twinkle twinkle little...?
Which one is the odd one out — which doesn't rhyme?

impact.text: Children hear and match rhyming words.
Children join in with and finish familiar nursery rhymes.
Children generate their own rhymes, including nonsense words.
Children spot the odd one out in a rhyming set.
Children learn and use new words from the basket.
Children delight in the rhythm and play of language.

enhancements: Nursery-rhyme prop bags — one basket per rhyme — to act them out.
A rhyming lotto or pairs game with picture cards.
A 'silly soup' pot: drop in objects that rhyme and stir up a rhyming spell.
Puppets who only understand you if you speak in rhyme.
A rhyme of the week displayed with actions to learn together.
Instruments to tap the beat and syllables of the rhymes.

playing_exploring: Children handle the objects and play freely with their sounds.
The silliness of nonsense rhymes invites them to experiment.
active_learning: Children keep hunting the basket to find the matching rhyme.
They join in rhymes again and again for the joy of it.
creating_thinking: Children hear the pattern and use it to make new rhymes.
They decide which words rhyme and which don't, and say why.
